Surya Namaskar is a sequence of 12 powerful yoga asanas [PROG_Y_001]. It is best performed early morning on an empty stomach [PROG_Y_001]. 

Ek complete round consists of two sets, starting with the right leg and then the left [PROG_Y_001]. Each posture is coordinated with your breath [PROG_Y_001]. People with high blood pressure, hernia, or back problems should consult a doctor or certified instructor before performing it [PROG_Y_001].

Anulom Vilom Pranayama karne se mind calm hota hai aur stress relieve hota hai [PROG_P_001]. Ye body me Tridoshas (Vata, Pitta, Kapha) ko balance karne me help karta hai aur patience and concentration ko improve karta hai [PROG_P_001].

Healthy lifestyle ke liye balanced diet zaroori hai jisme carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, aur minerals hon [PROG_D_001]. 

Breakfast mein fried foods ki jagah poha, upma, ya idli lein [PROG_D_001]. Lunch mein 2 rotis, ek bowl dal, sabzi, aur salad khayein [PROG_D_001]. Dinner sabse halka hona chahiye, jisme khichdi ya dal ke sath vegetable stir-fry ek accha option hai [PROG_D_001]. 

Snacking ke liye nuts aur seeds cravings manage karne ka ek great tarika hai [PROG_D_001]. Daily kam se kam 8-10 glasses paani (water) zaroor piyein aur processed sugar aur excessive salt se bachein [PROG_D_001].

Kapalbhati, or Skull Shining Breath, is an invigorating pranayama that cleanses the body through active, forceful exhalation and passive inhalation [PROG_P_002]. Sit comfortably with a straight spine, take a deep breath in, and exhale in short, powerful bursts while your stomach pumps inwards [PROG_P_002]. Start with a round of 20-30 pumps and do up to 3 rounds with breaks [PROG_P_002]. 

It stimulates the digestive system, improves metabolic rate, and aids in weight loss [PROG_P_002]. Perform it on an empty stomach, preferably in the morning [PROG_P_002]. Avoid this practice if you are pregnant, have high blood pressure, heart disease, hernia, or epilepsy [PROG_P_002].

Trikonasana, or Triangle Pose, is a foundational standing pose that stretches the entire body [PROG_Y_003]. To do it, stand with your feet wide apart, turn your right foot out 90 degrees and your left foot in slightly, then bend from the hips to extend your torso to the right [PROG_Y_003]. Place your right hand on your shin, ankle, or the floor, and extend your left arm up to the sky [PROG_Y_003]. It stretches the hamstrings, hips, and spine while strengthening the legs and core, and improves digestion [PROG_Y_003]. Hold for 30-60 seconds, but avoid it if you have a headache, low blood pressure, or a neck injury [PROG_Y_003].

Garmi ke liye aap Sheetali Pranayama (Cooling Breath) kar sakte hain. Yeh breathing technique body aur mind par cooling effect deti hai aur hot weather mein perfect hai [PROG_P_004]. 

Comfortable baith kar apni tongue ko tube shape mein roll karein aur mouth se bahar nikal kar straw ki tarah slow aur deep inhale karein [PROG_P_004]. Phir tongue andar karke mouth close karein aur nostrils se slow exhale karein [PROG_P_004]. Isko 5-10 times repeat karein [PROG_P_004]. Yeh body ko cool karta hai aur mental aur emotional excitation ko kam karta hai [PROG_P_004]. 

Note: Low blood pressure ya asthma jaise respiratory issues wale logon ke liye yeh recommended nahi hai [PROG_P_004].

Immunity ko boost karne ke liye ek balanced diet lena zaroori hai. Citrus fruits jaise amla, oranges, aur lemons mein Vitamin C hota hai jo immunity badhata hai [PROG_D_002]. Turmeric (haldi) mein curcumin hota hai, ise milk ya curries mein add karein [PROG_D_002]. Ginger aur garlic bhi bahut faydemand hain [PROG_D_002]. 

Yogurt probiotics ka achha source hai jo gut health ke liye achha hai [PROG_D_002]. Green leafy vegetables jaise spinach (palak) antioxidants se bhari hoti hain aur almonds Vitamin E ka achha source hain [PROG_D_002].

Yogi Devvrat is a certified RYT 500 Yoga Alliance instructor with over 15 years of experience, having started his journey in Rishikesh with traditional yoga gurus [PROG_I_001]. 

His teaching style blends classical Hatha yoga with modern Vinyasa flow, focusing on alignment, breath, pranayama, and meditation [PROG_I_001]. He specializes in therapeutic yoga to help manage chronic pain and stress-related ailments, believing that yoga is a way of life and famously stating, "Yoga ek yatra hai, manzil nahi" [PROG_I_001].

Millets are ancient grains that are gluten-free and rich in fiber, protein, and antioxidants [PROG_D_004]. They are considered a modern superfood for a healthy lifestyle [PROG_D_004]. 

Different types offer unique benefits, such as Ragi (Finger Millet) being an excellent source of calcium for bone health, Jowar (Sorghum) being packed with iron and protein, and Bajra (Pearl Millet) being rich in magnesium for heart health [PROG_D_004]. They also have a low glycemic index, making them suitable for diabetics, and their high fiber content aids in weight management [PROG_D_004].

To relax, you can practice Shavasana (Corpse Pose) by lying flat on your back with feet apart and arms by your sides, palms up [PROG_Y_004]. Close your eyes, release breath control, and bring awareness to your body to release tension (*thakaan*) [PROG_Y_004]. Spend 5-10 minutes to calm the nervous system and combat insomnia [PROG_Y_004]. 

Alternatively, try Balasana (Childs Pose) by kneeling, sitting back on your heels, and folding forward with your forehead on the floor [PROG_Y_005]. Hold for 30 seconds to a few minutes with deep diaphragmatic breathing to relieve stress, fatigue, and back or neck pain [PROG_Y_005].

Dia Malik is a certified clinical nutritionist with a Masters degree in Food and Nutrition [PROG_I_002]. She has helped over 500 clients reach their health goals, including weight management and managing conditions like PCOS and diabetes through diet [PROG_I_002]. Her philosophy focuses on a no-deprivation approach, creating sustainable diet plans that fit your lifestyle, cultural eating habits, and Indian cuisine [PROG_I_002]. You can book a one-on-one consultation with her to create a khaane ka plan (eating plan) tailored to your body's needs [PROG_I_002]. She is available on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 4 PM to 6 PM [PROG_I_002].

Staying hydrated is crucial for overall health as water regulates body temperature, lubricates joints, and delivers nutrients to cells [PROG_D_003]. Aim for 8-10 glasses of water per day, and sip it throughout the day rather than waiting until you are thirsty [PROG_D_003]. Drinking water before meals can aid in weight management, while proper hydration also supports kidney function and flushes out toxins [PROG_D_003].
